title: Dates and times
game_role: When the game opens, your daily streak is calculated.
objective: Create dates with the datetime module, format them and calculate between dates
story: We've landed on Discovery Island! In the middle of the island stands a giant sundial with a message: "Whoever reads time will solve the island's secret." Daily rewards, streaks and countdowns in games all run on date math. Today we read time with Python.

sections.title: The datetime module
sections.body:
For dates and times we use the `datetime` module. We'll mostly use three of its parts:

```python
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

today = date.today()      # today's date
now = datetime.now()      # the current date and time
```

`date.today()` gives a different result every day. That's why the tasks use fixed dates.

sections.title: Creating a date
sections.body:
```python
birthday = date(2014, 5, 19)   # year, month, day
print(birthday.year)    # 2014
print(birthday.month)   # 5
print(birthday.day)     # 19
print(birthday.weekday())  # 0 Monday ... 6 Sunday
```

If you need the time too, write `datetime(2026, 9, 23, 14, 30)`: 2:30 pm.

sections.title: Formatting
sections.body:
`strftime` turns a date into text in the format you want:

- `%d` day, `%m` month (number), `%B` month name, `%Y` four-digit year
- `%H` hour, `%M` minute

```python
d = date(2026, 9, 23)
print(d.strftime("%d %B %Y"))   # 23 September 2026
print(d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))   # 2026-09-23
```

`datetime.strptime("2026-09-23", "%Y-%m-%d")` does the opposite: it makes a date from text.

sections.title: Calculating with dates
sections.body:
Subtracting two dates gives the time between them. `.days` gives you the number of days:

```python
start = date(2026, 9, 1)
end = date(2026, 9, 30)
print((end - start).days)   # 29
```

To add days to a date, use `timedelta`:

```python
print(start + timedelta(days=7))   # one week later
```

examples.title: Parts of a date
examples.code:
from datetime import date

d = date(2026, 9, 23)
print("Year:", d.year)
print("Month:", d.month)
print("Day:", d.day)
print(d.strftime("%d %B %Y"))

examples.title: How many days left?
examples.code:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
new_year = date(2027, 1, 1)
left = (new_year - today).days
print(f"{left} days until the new year.")

examples.title: A week later
examples.code:
from datetime import date, timedelta

start = date(2026, 9, 23)
for week in range(1, 4):
    print(f"Week {week}:", (start + timedelta(days=7 * week)).strftime("%d %B %Y"))

tasks.title: Format the date
tasks.prompt: Create a date from `year`, `month` and `day` and print it as `23 September 2026`.
tasks.starter:
from datetime import date

year = 2026
month = 9
day = 23

# create the date and print it as day month-name year
tasks.solution:
from datetime import date

year = 2026
month = 9
day = 23

d = date(year, month, day)
print(d.strftime("%d %B %Y"))

tasks.title: How many days left?
tasks.prompt: Store the number of days between `today` and the `birthday` in `days_left` and print something like `12 days until your birthday.`
tasks.starter:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
birthday_day = 5
birthday = date(2026, 10, birthday_day)

days_left = 0

print(f"{days_left} days until your birthday.")
tasks.solution:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
birthday_day = 5
birthday = date(2026, 10, birthday_day)

days_left = (birthday - today).days

print(f"{days_left} days until your birthday.")
hints: Subtract the two dates: birthday - today
Add .days to get the number of days.

tasks.title: A week later
tasks.prompt: Add `weeks` weeks to the `start` date and print the result in `day month-name year` format.
tasks.starter:
from datetime import date, timedelta

start = date(2026, 9, 23)
weeks = 1

# start + weeks weeks
tasks.solution:
from datetime import date, timedelta

start = date(2026, 9, 23)
weeks = 1

later = start + timedelta(weeks=weeks)
print(later.strftime("%d %B %Y"))

challenge.title: Day of the week
challenge.prompt: `weekday()` gives a number from 0 (Monday) to 6 (Sunday). Use that number with the `names` list to print which day the date is: `23 September 2026 Wednesday`
challenge.starter:
from datetime import date

names = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
year, month, day = 2026, 9, 23
d = date(year, month, day)

# print the date and the day's name
challenge.solution:
from datetime import date

names = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
year, month, day = 2026, 9, 23
d = date(year, month, day)

print(d.strftime("%d %B %Y"), names[d.weekday()])

project_task.title: Daily streak
project_task.prompt:
In games your streak grows if you play every day. `last_play` is the last day you played, `today` is today.

- If the difference is 0 days: `You already played today.`
- If it's 1 day: `Your streak continues!`
- If it's more: `Streak broken, start again!`
project_task.starter:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
last_day = 22
last_play = date(2026, 9, last_day)

# calculate the difference and print the message
project_task.solution:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
last_day = 22
last_play = date(2026, 9, last_day)

gap = (today - last_play).days
if gap == 0:
    print("You already played today.")
elif gap == 1:
    print("Your streak continues!")
else:
    print("Streak broken, start again!")
